_provenance.purpose: Reference data for the extrinsic evaluation harness (eval_grounding_overlap.py), decision #49 in memory/decisions.md. Rebuilt 2026-09-25 (Claude Code) after the original extrinsic_eval_harness_2026-08-31.zip was found to have never been committed to this repo -- reconstructed strictly from decision #49's spec plus the coded source material in FOR_CASSIE_AUGUST_2026_V4-TAXONOMY/03_SECTION_4.6_PRODUCTION_EVAL/external_reference_curricula.md and chatbot/data/program_and_curriculum/queens-university-mmai.txt.
_provenance.no_llm_judge: Every skill list below was coded by hand from the cited source material -- no LLM was used to generate, summarize, or judge these lists, consistent with the harness's core design goal (answers the paper's own §7 circularity concern).
_provenance.attested_set_size_note: 73 associated skills clear z>=2 for focal skill 'Agentic Ai' in chatbot/data/skill_lift_table.csv as of 2026-09-25 -- confirmed via `awk -F',' 'tolower($1)=="agentic ai" && $7+0>=2' chatbot/data/skill_lift_table.csv | wc -l`. This is the GROUNDING reference set; it is computed live by eval_grounding_overlap.py from --lift, not hardcoded here.
_provenance.open_todo_flagged_not_decided: external_reference_curricula.md's 'Target: the paper's lift-derived agentic curriculum' section lists 'model providers / serving' and 'agent evaluation' as skills the chatbot's curriculum SHOULD cover -- neither is literally an attested (z>=2) Agentic Ai association in skill_lift_table.csv (closest real attested neighbours: 'Model Deployment' z=2.13, 'Model Evaluation' z=2.28, 'LLMOps' z=2.27, 'Ai Engineering' z=4.33 -- none is an exact or obvious-alias match). Preserved verbatim below as `target_skills_for_context` for narrative/paper-writing reference ONLY -- eval_grounding_overlap.py does NOT read or score against this field; grounding is computed solely from the live z>=2 attested set. Claude Code's recommendation (Eric to confirm, not silently decided): keep both OUT of anything the scorer treats as 'attested' -- the whole point of the z>=2 bar is strict quantitative rigor, and 'Model Providers/Serving' and 'Agent Evaluation' are genuinely close-but-not-identical to real attested neighbours, so folding them in would quietly loosen the bar. They remain legitimate to mention qualitatively in the paper's prose/caveats (the same 'no lift/z available, included on frequency/qualitative grounds' honesty pattern already used elsewhere in this project's chatbot output), just not counted toward a quantitative grounding percentage.
